A landing page structure that helps visitors decide

Build the page around a single offer and the questions it creates.

NITESH PATEL · WEB DEVELOPMENT NOTES · 2026

Build the page around a single offer and the questions it creates. This guide looks at the decisions that matter before and after the page goes live.

Start with the real need

The opening screen should tell the right visitor what is offered and what to do next. A vague slogan makes people work harder to understand whether the page is for them.

Plan the structure

Follow with the information needed to decide: what is included, who it is for, examples of the result, process and common questions. Put the strongest proof close to the claims it supports.

Make practical choices

Use one main action consistently. The page can repeat the action after meaningful sections, but it should not introduce competing goals at every turn.

Check the result

Check the page on a phone, where reading space is limited. Keep forms short, labels visible and buttons easy to tap. Measure completed enquiries rather than clicks alone.

Apply this to your own site

Start with the page your visitors use most. Review its purpose, the questions it answers and the action it supports. Then make one measurable improvement at a time.
